extracted.intended_audience: high-school-aged writers (teen writers) and their parents/guardians considering a summer creative-writing program
extracted.subtask_description: Information and requirements for applying to and attending the Sewanee Young Writers Conference (SYWC): program dates, costs, required application materials, program offerings, workshop structure, faculty qualities, enrichment activities, and student support/community life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Course offerings: Fiction, poetry, creative nonfiction, and playwriting

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply, you'll need: A writing sample, a personal statement, and a letter of recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation form is available via a provided link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timeline and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications: Open December 2025 and close March 2nd, 2026. We will notify you of our decision in the first week of April.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon acceptance, prospective participants will be provided with a link to the financial aid application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial aid availability and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial aid: Prospective participants will be provided with a link to the financial aid application upon acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate page/link is provided to learn more about financial aid opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: A remarkable faculty who love to write and teach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty have won literary prizes, been recognized by major publications (New York Times, The New Yorker), and have experience working with teenagers in the classroom; they are writers who love to teach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop structure and rigor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops meet from 9:30–12:30 every morning except Sunday; no more than twelve students per workshop; total enrollment about eighty-five young writers; schedule includes one-on-one conferences between students and teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrichment and afternoon programming
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Afternoon opportunities include Q&As with special-guest authors, a tour of the Sewanee Review, short craft classes on topics from sonnets to zines, and free time to write, read, and think. Every evening includes a faculty or guest reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative support and student safety
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative staff support students throughout the conference—ensuring safety, addressing needs, and providing help from workshops through end of day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community and extracurricular life
rubrics_metrics.description: Fun — community activities and social life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunities include socializing on the porch swing at Stirling's, visiting a coffee house, swimming and playing basketball at the Fowler Sports and Recreation Center, hiking Sewanee’s trails, karaoke night, and board games in dorm common rooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions? Call or email for more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phone: 931-598-1541; Email: sywc@sewanee.edu — staff will respond as soon as possible.
